name: Services & Process Management
description: Manage services, processes, scheduled tasks (cron/at), and systemd units, timers, and transient runs

operations.name: status
operations.description: Get status of a service including recent logs

operations.name: enable
operations.description: Enable a service to start on boot

operations.name: disable
operations.description: Disable a service from starting on boot

operations.name: logs
operations.description: View logs for a service or the system journal

operations.name: processes
operations.description: List or manage running processes — find, inspect, or kill processes

operations.name: cron
operations.description: Manage cron jobs — list, add, edit, or remove scheduled tasks

skill_config.system_prompt: You are a service and process management agent. For services, use 'systemctl status SERVICE' and 'journalctl -u SERVICE --no-pager -n LINES'. Always use --no-pager with journalctl. When restarting, check status before and after. If a service fails, check its logs. For processes, use 'ps aux', 'top -bn1', or 'pgrep'. Before killing, identify what the process is. For cron: list with 'crontab -l', add with '(crontab -l 2>/dev/null; echo "SCHEDULE COMMAND") | crontab -'. Also check /etc/cron.d/, /etc/crontab, and systemd timers with 'systemctl list-timers'.

quick_reports.label: Service Inventory
quick_reports.instruction: List the systemd service units that are currently running (systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running --no-pager --no-legend), then the ones that are enabled but not running (systemctl list-unit-files --type=service --state=enabled --no-pager --no-legend). In the summary give both counts. Keep the output to those two commands: do not list every installed unit file, and do not run follow-up commands on individual services.

quick_reports.label: Failed Services
quick_reports.instruction: List the systemd units in failed state (systemctl list-units --state=failed --no-pager). Name every failed unit in the summary and give the count. Read the count off the output itself — only report zero failed units if the output lists none. Do not run follow-up commands on individual services.
